title: 3 days PPL program review
summary: NH reviews a viewer's 3-day push/pull/legs program. He objects to rotating lifts with very different tonnage (bench vs overhead press, deadlift vs rows), wants both presses on every push day as 3x5, keeps deadlifts and rows together on pull day, swaps lat pulldowns for pull-ups, and suggests supersets, hip thrusts and actually doing calves.

claims.claim: Presses benefit from high frequency: do presses at least twice a week, and do both a vertical and a horizontal press on every press day.
High-frequency horizontal pressing taxes the shoulder mostly through tendon stress, while vertical pressing causes more muscular damage.

Bench press and overhead press should not be rotated with each other: they aren't similar enough in specificity, and their large tonnage difference makes tonnage stability impossible, especially on a 5x5.
A suboptimal rep scheme doesn't fix a suboptimal frequency; with push once a week, do bench 3x5 and overhead press 3x5 (30 total reps) rather than alternating 5x5s.
NH doesn't like 5x5, though within a once-a-week push frequency it isn't terrible because you need the volume.
Incline bench 3x8-10 is a good follow-up to either bench or overhead press since it is a mix of vertical and horizontal pressing.
Cable flies 3-4x12 are a fine pump/squeeze movement for the chest.
Lateral raises can be used heavily without hurting the shoulders if done properly, which most people don't; supersetting them with triceps extensions is a good pairing.
Include an overhead/behind-the-head triceps extension to train the long head; not forgetting the long head is a strength of a push day.
If you want more visible shoulder caps, overhead press on every press day and consider raising press frequency; add the optional 4th day as a push day most of the time.
In program reviews NH respects the template's frequency and doesn't change it.
Alternating deadlifts and bent-over rows isn't rotating lifts but rotating programs; with proper form you should row barely half your deadlift, so tonnage discrepancy is even worse.
Deadlift 3x5 is not the best rep range for progression but is a good volume for pulls from the floor, especially with high intensity.
Bent-over rows at 8-10 reps allow proper form and upper-back involvement.
Instead of lat pulldowns, do pull-ups: more athletic, more lat stretch, less spinal loading, and faster progression; use the machine only if you like the pump.
Cable row is one of NH's favourite machine movements.
Dumbbell shrugs at 3x12-15 is an excellent rep range; doubling shrug sets to 6 via supersets adds upper-back and trap volume without much fatigue.
For maintaining already-big biceps, high intensity and low volume is the way: EZ-bar curls at 6-8 reps are heavy enough not to be fluff.

Don't skip deadlifts when you only pull once or twice a week; if lower-back volume is too much, do deadlift 3x1 then rows. A pull from the floor every 7 days with good form shouldn't be too taxing to repeat.
Superset pulls with curls (e.g. pull-ups with EZ curls, cable rows with hammer curls) to save time and add volume.
A PPL weakness: deadlifts on pull day can leave the posterior chain tired for back squats on leg day.
NH finds back squats more taxing than deadlifts, so when two heavy lower compound days are close together he puts deadlifts first and squats second.
Back squat 4x4-6 is a functional evolving rep range: not heavy enough that the squat turns into a good morning, not so heavy it becomes hard to recover from.
Supplemental lifts you don't care to progress on (e.g. lunges by feel, NH's own pull-ups) don't need to be counted or tracked.
Rotating lifts should be close in nature: leg curls vs RDL is better than bench vs OHP but still mixes isolation and compound; RDL and stiff-leg deadlift is a much better rotation.
3x8-12 is an excellent rep range for hip hinges like the Romanian deadlift.
NH doesn't like leg extensions but accepts them if you like them for quads.
Calf work done 'if I feel like it' at the end of a session never gets done; NH admits he was the same.
Hip thrusts can rotate with Romanian deadlifts: both are hip hinges working glutes and hamstrings; hip thrusts emphasise quads more, RDLs the lower back.
Superset leg extensions with leg curls to end leg day with a pump, and add 25-rep calf raises after each superset so calves actually get trained.
